title: Interest on Reserve Balances (IORB) — Current Rate
summary: The Interest on Reserve Balances (IORB) rate stands at 3.65% as of April 27, 2026, unchanged from the prior observation on April 26. The rate has remained flat at 3.65% across all observed dates from April 23–27, 2026, indicating stable Fed policy settings in the current observation window.
key_points: Absolute change: 0 (flat) over the observed period
Rate has been flat at 3.65% from April 23–27, 2026 (5 consecutive observations)
IORB is the interest rate the Federal Reserve pays on reserves held by depository institutions at Fed banks
IORB serves as the primary policy rate tool in the current Fed operating framework, setting the floor for the federal funds rate
why_it_matters: IORB is the key policy rate in the Fed's current operating framework, directly influencing banks' cost of capital and incentive to lend or hold reserves. A flat IORB indicates the Fed is maintaining its current policy stance without signaling imminent rate changes. This rate directly impacts short-term funding markets, money market fund yields, and repo market dynamics, making it essential for monitoring monetary policy direction and market liquidity conditions.
market_structure_context: IORB functions as the floor rate in the Fed's interest-on-reserves regime, which began post-2008 financial crisis. When the Fed raised rates in the 2022–2023 cycle, IORB moved in lockstep with the federal funds rate target, making it the primary operational target. Banks have less incentive to lend in the fed funds market below IORB, effectively anchoring short-term rates and influencing repo market dynamics. The stability of IORB at 3.65% suggests no pending changes to the Fed's monetary policy operations or balance sheet management approach.
